plan.melodySummary: The tune bounces playfully from Flute to Clarinet to Viola and finally to Tuba, each handing off fragments across section boundaries with staccato pops and cheeky grace notes. Dynamics climb from a light !mp! opening through a bright !f! peak in mm.9-12, then wink back down to a clipped !mf! finish.

sections.label: Verse A
sections.notes: Skip out the theme !mp! light staccato, tiny grace note into each phrase, clip the final D short

sections.label: Verse A repeat
sections.notes: Take the tune !mf! bouncy and cheeky, Flute tosses back echo fragments, surprise rest on the last bar

sections.label: Chorus
sections.notes: Sing out the refrain !f! at the high point, spirited and detached, quick ornamental turn on the F-G figure

sections.label: Chorus finale
sections.notes: Grab the melody !mf! with a big grinning oom-pah swagger, Flute sprinkles staccato descant, clip the last note off

Flute.instruction: Lead brightly in the opening then become the sparkling top-voice descant elsewhere — grace notes, quick turns, staccato dabs !mp!-!f!, always tossing playful echoes

Clarinet.instruction: Take the tune cheekily in the second verse; elsewhere supply off-beat oom-pah chirps and hiccup syncopations, keeping harmony crisp and detached

Viola.instruction: Provide bouncing off-beat pizzicato-style chords when accompanying, then step forward with a warm !f! chorus melody; hold the low harmony ground when Tuba sings

Tuba.instruction: Anchor a springy oom-pah bass through most of the piece with varied walking approaches, then grab the finale melody with grinning swagger while Viola covers the bass

groundTruth.melodyNotes: Melody begins with a quarter-note pickup (anacrusis) on the words 'Yankee Doodle went to town'; strophic form where verse and chorus (refrain, 'Yankee Doodle keep it up') share the same tune and chord pattern. Rhythm is march-like with dotted-eighth/sixteenth figures typical of fife tunes. Melodic range spans roughly one octave (G to G), with a rising contour into the phrase 'riding on a pony' and a characteristic falling cadence at 'macaroni'.
